Pair of plates 
England, mid 18th century 
Tin-glazed earthenware, diameter 21.6 cm (below), 20.8 cm (right) 
Asian Civilisations Museum, 2007-55836, 2007-55835 
Gift of Mr and Mrs Toubou Egawa 
Tin-glazed earthenware produced in England was also known as dellware, because the decoration was painted in the style of ceramics from Dell. The scenes on both plates are fine interpretations rather than lavish copies of actual Chinese designs. The decoration has been attempted to create figures that look Chinese by depicting them with Chinese-style robes and setting them in landscapes derived from Chinese porcelain. The pagoda and the Asian-style parasol were also meant to evoke the East.
